summary: A roughly 3 km guided loop through mossy cloud forest and exposed mountain grassland in Doi Inthanon National Park. Shortlist it for a proper mountain walk and changing ecosystems; panoramic views depend on weather.
whyGo: Cool, fern-filled forest opens abruptly onto a grassy ridge above the valleys.
A local community guide accompanies each group; the walk offers more immersion than roadside viewpoints.
bestFor: Moderately active walkers and landscape photographers
Travellers already planning a full Doi Inthanon day
skipIf: Stairs, uneven ground or exposed slopes are uncomfortable
You want guaranteed clear views or a short outing from central Chiang Mai
duration: Allow 2–3 hours on the loop, plus roughly two hours driving each way from Chiang Mai; reserve most of a day.
cost: Planning allowance from independent visitor guides: foreign-adult park entry 300 THB plus mandatory local guide around 200 THB per group. Transport and any vehicle admission extra. Current official tariffs and guide group limit were not verified.
hours: Independent guides report 06:00–16:00 during November–May; usually closed June–October. Confirm current opening and latest permitted start before travelling.
bestTime: Cool-season morning, ideally beginning by 08:00, for quieter paths and a chance of cloud-filled valleys.
gettingThere: Trailhead near km 42 on the Doi Inthanon summit road. Hire a driver/car or choose a tour explicitly including this hike; arrange return transport rather than depending on an on-demand mountain pickup.
booking: Local guide hired at the trailhead. Ask a day-tour operator whether the full Kew Mae Pan loop, guide and park admission are included; many park tours omit this longer walk.
accessibility: Not wheelchair accessible: uphill stairs, dirt, potentially slippery sections and narrow ridge paths. Requires sustained walking despite the relatively short distance.
practicalTips: Carry cash, drinking water and shoes with grip.
Pack warm layers and a rain shell; exposed ridge weather differs from the city.
Agree a comfortable pace with the guide and stay on marked paths.
decemberNotes: December falls within the usual operating season and is popular. Expect cold mountain mornings and heavier weekend/holiday traffic. Mist can create spectacular scenes or obscure the view entirely; check the forecast and operational notice shortly before the trip.
uncertainties: The report-linked DNP page could not be fetched; December 2026 opening is not officially confirmed here.
Independent sources differ on guide group limits and exact trail distance. Current fees, last entry and any weather closures require confirmation.
